title: Concentrated Liquidity (CLMM)
objectives: Understand why concentrated liquidity (CLMM) is far more capital-efficient than a full-range AMM
Choose a price range and see how it multiplies your fee-earning power
See what happens to your position when price exits your range
Read the real trade-off: higher fees when in range, but total impermanent loss to one side when out of range

steps.title: Your Pro Sandbox
steps.text: This is a concentrated-liquidity desk. You will pack capital into a narrow band and watch what happens when price leaves it.

steps.title: Module Badge
steps.text: LAB P7 marks the CLMM range lab. Reset restores the default range and price move.

steps.title: Range & Efficiency
steps.text: Dial your capital, range width and price move. The bar shows whether price stayed inside your tick range - in range earns fees, out of range earns nothing.

steps.title: What Just Happened?
steps.text: Concentration multiplies fees AND impermanent loss - the explainer spells out which side of that trade-off you are on.

steps.title: Why Concentration Changes Everything
steps.body:
A classic <Term id="amm">AMM</Term> spreads your liquidity across **every possible price** from $0 to infinity - even prices the token will never trade at. Almost all of that capital sits idle, doing nothing, earning nothing.

Concentrated liquidity (CLMM, as on Orca) lets you say: 'I only want to provide liquidity between $140 and $160.' Your entire deposit is now packed into that narrow band. Inside the range, your money is enormously dense - it captures a much larger share of every swap than the same capital spread across all prices.

**The capital-efficiency idea in one image:**

- Full-range LP: one drop of liquidity smeared over a football field.
- Concentrated LP: that same drop focused into a square meter - where the game is actually being played.

The efficiency multiplier is roughly `fullRangeWidth / yourRangeWidth`. Provide a range that is 1/10th as wide, and you may earn ~10x the fees on the same deposit *while price stays inside*. That 'while' is the entire catch, and it is where concentration bites back.
hints: Concentration = same money, far smaller price band, way more fee share. Efficiency ≈ fullWidth / yourWidth.
The magic lasts ONLY while price is inside your chosen range.

steps.title: When You Are Right, and When You Are Rekt
steps.body:
A concentrated position is a bet that price will **stay inside your band**. Play the two outcomes:

**Price stays in range:**

- Your liquidity is active and dense, so you earn a large share of fees.
- As price wiggles across the band, your position rebalances between the two tokens.
- You outperform a full-range LP by a wide margin.

**Price exits your range - and stays out:**

- Your position stops earning fees entirely, because no swap crosses your band.
- Your position becomes **100% one token**: all the token that fell, if price dropped below your range; all the token that rose, if price broke above.
- You are now exactly like the person who simply held the losing asset - you missed the up-move because you converted into the wrong side and then sat frozen.

This is the deepest trap of CLMM. People chase the eye-popping APR in a narrow range, then price trends away, and they are left holding a lopsided bag that earns **zero** while the token runs without them. The fee yield and the <Term id="impermanent_loss">impermanent loss</Term> are two faces of the same choice: the tighter the range, the more you earn when right and the more violently you are wrong when not. Concentration does not remove risk. It swaps a little-of-everything risk for an all-or-nothing risk at your chosen boundary.
hints: In range = dense liquidity = big fee share. Out of range = zero fees + 100% exposure to one token.
Tight ranges supercharge fees AND supercharge impermanent loss. There is no free efficiency.

steps.title: Under the Hood: Ticks, Ranges, and Active Liquidity
steps.body:
A CLMM does not store one giant `x * y = k` pool. It divides the price axis into **ticks**, and each position declares which ticks it covers. At any moment, only the liquidity whose range contains the *current* tick is 'active' - that is what the swap trades against.

Two consequences follow directly from this design:

- **Fee share is per-tick.** When price passes through your range, your liquidity counts. When price is outside, your liquidity is invisible to the swap, so it earns nothing.
- **Position composition is range-relative.** As price moves within your band, your position swaps between token A and token B to stay balanced at the edge of the curve. Push price to the top of your range and you are ~100% of the 'sold' token; push it to the bottom and you are ~100% of the other. This is why an out-of-range position behaves like a frozen spot holding.

Professionals treat range selection as a *market view*, not a settings screen. A wide range is a slow, steady, lower-yield position close to full-range LP. A razor-thin range is a high-conviction bet that pays spectacularly for a short window and can leave you holding the wrong asset the moment you are wrong. The <Term id="tvl">TVL</Term> headline hides this: much of a CLMM's TVL may be inactive at the current price, earning nothing at all.
hints: Only the liquidity covering the current tick trades. Outside your range = invisible capital.
Out-of-range position ≈ 100% of one token, frozen, earning zero fees.

questions.prompt: Why is a concentrated liquidity position more capital-efficient than a full-range one?
options: It uses more tokens per deposit
The same capital is packed into a narrow price band, so it captures a much larger share of swaps while price is inside the range
It is guaranteed to earn more than full-range LP
questions.explainRight: Correct. Full-range spreads capital thinly across all prices; concentration focuses it where trading actually happens. Inside the range, your money is dense - so it commands a much bigger share of fees. That efficiency scales inversely with range width.
questions.explainWrong: It is not about depositing more tokens - it is about density. Concentrating the SAME capital into a narrow band gives it a large share of swap fees within that band. The trade-off is that the advantage disappears once price leaves the range.

questions.prompt: Price breaks ABOVE your chosen range and stays there. What is your position doing?
options: Still earning the maximum fees because it is concentrated
Earning zero fees and sitting almost entirely in the other token - effectively a frozen spot holding that missed the up-move
Automatically widening its range to keep earning
questions.explainRight: Correct. Out of range, no swap crosses your ticks, so you earn nothing. Your position has converted to ~100% of the token price moved against, meaning you missed the rally in the asset you wanted. You are frozen until price returns or you rebalance.
questions.explainWrong: Concentration only pays while price is inside. Break above and your liquidity goes inactive: zero fees, and your holdings are skewed to ~100% of the weak side. You effectively sat out the move - the classic out-of-range frustration.

questions.prompt: You want maximum fee yield for a short window because you are very confident price stays put. What range do you choose, and what is the risk?
options: A very wide range; the only risk is low fees
A very tight range; the risk is that price exits quickly and you stop earning with heavy impermanent loss
A full range; the risk is being liquidated
No range; CLMM positions do not have ranges
questions.explainRight: Correct. A tight range maximizes fee share and efficiency while price cooperates - but the moment price breaks out, you stop earning and your position is lopsided with elevated IL. High reward, high fragility. It is a directional bet dressed as yield.
questions.explainWrong: Maximum short-term yield comes from the tightest sensible range. The flip side is extreme fragility: any breakout puts you out of range with zero fees and concentrated impermanent loss. Wide ranges are the lower-yield, lower-variance choice.

questions.prompt: A protocol advertises a huge TVL and eye-popping CLMM APRs. What is the most important thing to check?
options: Nothing - high TVL always means safe yields
How much of that liquidity is actually IN RANGE at the current price, since out-of-range capital earns nothing and the headline APR may not be achievable
Only the token's logo and brand
Whether the pool uses a wallet
questions.explainRight: Correct. Headline TVL counts all deposited capital, but only the liquidity covering the current tick earns. A pool can show massive TVL while most of it sits inactive out of range. Real, achievable yield depends on in-range depth and your own range choice.
questions.explainWrong: TVL is a vanity-ish total that includes inactive liquidity. Because CLMM capital only earns while in range, the advertised APR can be far above what a new depositor actually realizes. The question to ask is: how much liquidity is active right here, right now?
